newsitem.title: THAILAND: Former Thai prime minister Chatichai in hospital.
newsitem.headline: Former Thai prime minister Chatichai in hospital.

text.p: Former prime minister Chatichai Choonhavan, currently top economic and foreign affairs adviser to the new Thai government, has been operated on for stomach cancer, an aide said on Thursday.
"He underwent stomach surgery and his condition is stable, he is safe," the aide told Reuters, dispelling rumours that he was in a critical condition.

Talk that former premier Chatichai, 76, had been admitted to hospital had a negative effect on the stock market, which tumbled by more than two percent in early trading. The market was also down because of foreign investor selling, brokers said.
They added that players in the market were concerned that Chatichai's hospitalisation could affect the new government's economic recovery plans for the slowing Thai economy.
Chatichai has been mainly charged with luring foreign investment into Thailand.

He is the head of the Chart Pattana party, which is the second-largest component in the new six-party coalition government of Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, which assumed power in early-December.
Chatichai was hospitalised on Tuesday, the aide said.
He was prime minister from 1989 to February 1991 when his government was overthrown in a bloodless military coup.
